operator_io_quirks: All identifiers lowercase, no spaces; still double-quote in generated SQL per spec.

geographic.city is TEXT PK with 168 distinct values; generalinfo.city/location.city FK to it but only 167/165 distinct -> some parents unreferenced, some children may reference missing parents in original (FK not enforced).
location has TWO FKs: id_restaurant->generalinfo (1:1-ish, 9539 vs 9590) and city->geographic; both must be filled from parent final columns.
generalinfo.id_restaurant and location.id_restaurant are INTEGER PKs, distinct=rows -> no PK duplicates in original; TS Number fuzzer will produce duplicates that get dropped.
review is REAL with only 33 distinct values in [2.3,4.0]; TS Number(scale from 'real' -> no args -> scale default) will draw wide floats, not this range.
street_num INTEGER with 4.8% NULLs and 3966 distinct; TS Number will not reproduce NULLs (upstream doesn't enforce NOT NULL, but nullable columns still get non-null draws).
No declared type dispatches to crash fallback; all map to String or Number cleanly.
No text-stored dates, no composite keys, no self-references, no dangling FKs, no non-unique parents.
geographic.county/region have 0% NULL but are nullable; TS may emit NULLs there (insert succeeds).
Small tables (168/9590/9539 rows) -> read_schema full read, no rowid sampling needed.
label has 7606 distinct of 9590 (near-unique but not declared unique); TS String fuzzer will produce many duplicates -> no unique constraint so all kept.
food_type 145 distinct, city 167 distinct: low-cardinality strings; TS String fuzzer draws from CHARSET, not these values, unless literal pool supplies them.
operator_ts_expectations: geographic.city (TEXT PK, String fuzzer): random a-zA-Z0-9() strings of length 0-20, contaminated 50% -> implausible city names; PK dedup keeps first occurrence.
generalinfo.city / location.city (FK): drawn with replacement from geographic.city final values -> consistent, but many-to-one ties created (original has 167/165 distinct vs 168 parents).
location.id_restaurant (FK to generalinfo PK): drawn from generalinfo.id_restaurant final values -> 1:1-ish preserved but duplicates possible; location PK dedup then drops rows.
generalinfo.id_restaurant / location.id_restaurant (INTEGER PK, Number fuzzer): uniform ints in [-10^scale,10^scale] with +-1/+-2 perturbation -> huge ids, not 1..9590; PK dedup drops collisions.
review (REAL, Number): wide floats, not [2.3,4.0]; likely FN driver for AVG(review)/range predicates.
street_num (INTEGER, Number): wide ints, not 100-4000; FN for street_num predicates.
label/food_type/street_name (String): random charset strings, not real names -> FN for LIKE/equality on these; FP possible when random string accidentally matches a literal.
county/region (String, low cardinality): random strings, not 'bay area'/'napa county' -> FN for region/county filters.
Literal pool from train SQL will inject some real values (e.g. 'san francisco', 'afghani') into String samplers via elements, partially mitigating FN.
No CHECK constraints, no UNIQUE columns -> drop_unique_duplicates is a no-op; only PK dedup filters rows.
FK consistency means joins generalinfo-location-geographic always match on city/id_restaurant -> join cardinality plausible; misses come from value plausibility, not referential breaks.
Number fuzzer's list_max overwrite quirk: with literal-pool elements the upper bound resets to full range -> fresh draws ignore observed max, widening review/street_num beyond original.
